Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant.

2. Insurance Company has preferred this appeal against the Judgment and award of the Tribunal in MVC No.866/2017 dated 11.09.2018 passed by the Court of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T, Kalaburagi (for short 'the Tribunal').
3. One Ambika W/o Ravindra met with an accident on 14.08.2017.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Her children filed a claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.42,00,000/- with interest.

The Tribunal after considering entire evidence on record, NC: 2025:KHC-K:7423 HC-KAR granted an amount of 23,65,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

4. Aggrieved by the said order, Insurance Company has preferred this appeal in which it is contended that, the Tribunal granted excess amount of Rs.2,03,032/- towards Medical Expenses and thus, requested for reduction of the same.

Learned counsel for the appellant has contended that The Divisional Manager vs Ravindra And Ors on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27331773/
2 the Insurance Company objected for the said amount even before the Tribunal, but it was not considered by the Tribunal.
5.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Ravindra And Ors on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Inspite of service of notice, respondents did not turned up.

6. The Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.11,72,700/- towards medical expenses relying upon Ex.P10 - medical bills, which should be reduced by considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant.

Hence, this Court finds reasonable to reduce the total compensation from Rs.23,65,700/- to an extent NC: 2025:KHC-K:7423 HC-KAR of Rs.21,62,668/- i.e. medical expenses is reduced from Rs.11,72,700/- to Rs.9,69,668/-.
7.
In all, the total compensation comes to Rs.21,62,668/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

8. The award passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
 1. Love and affection 75,000/-
 2. Funeral expenses & transportation 15,000/-
 charges

3 . Loss of dependency 10,88,000/-
 4. Medical expenditure 9,69,668/-
 5. Loss of estate 15,000/-
 Total 21,62,668/-

Accordingly, the claimants are entitled for a reduced compensation of Rs.21,62,668/- against the award of the Tribunal i.e., Rs.23,65,700/-
9.

In the result, the following order is passed:
i) The appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7423 HC-KAR ii) The claimants are entitled for a reduced compensation of Rs.21,62,668/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

iii) Appellant's counsel stated that the Insurance Company has already deposited 50% of the award amount, therefore, the respondent - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the balance compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% within one month from the date of this order.
iv) On such, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount as per the apportionment of the tribunal.
